50690730.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to N-terminal His6-SUMO tagged recombinant human PDK2 by isothermal titration calorimetry
50690730.references_previous: Reference 39: Brautigam, C. A.; Zhao, H.; Vargas, C.; Keller, S.; Schuck, P. Integration and global analysis of isothermal titration calorimetry data for studying macromolecular interactions. Nat. Protoc. 2016, 11, 882–894.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: The SUMO-tagged PDK2 was dialyzed against 1 L of the dialysis buffer containing 50 mM MOPS, pH 7.0, 50 mM KCl, 1 mM MgCl2, and 0.5 mM β-mercaptoethanol. Ligand solutions (100–200 μM) were placed in the titration syringe and injected in 8 μL increments into the reaction cell containing 1.4 mL of 10–20 μM PDK2 at 15 °C in a VP-ITC microcalorimeter (GE Healthcare, Piscataway, NJ). Both protein and ligand were prepared in the dialysis buffer plus 4% of DMSO. All of the ITC data were initially analyzed by the NITPIC program39 to construct the baseline, followed by curve-fitting in Origin 7 to obtain binding parameters. The concentrations of SUMO-tagged PDK2 protein were determined by A280 and using calculated molar extinction coefficients (M−1·cm−1) of 49530.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Thermodynamic analysis of 1, 2, 5, and 17 binding to PDK2. Thermodynamic signatures of inhibitor binding were obtained by isothermo titration calorimetry using the Gibbs equation ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, where ΔG is Gibbs binding energy; ΔH, binding enthalpy; ΔS, binding entropy; T, absolute temperature. The derived dissociation constants (Kd) for 1, 2, 5, and 17 are 426, 156, 110, and 22 nM, respectively.
original_paragraph.Results section - ITC analysis: The binding of 1, 2, 5, and 17 to PDK2 were analyzed by isothermal calorimetry (ITC), producing dissociation constants (Kd) of 426, 156, 110, and 22 nM, respectively. The binding of these compounds to PDK2 is mainly enthalpy driven; however, the higher binding affinity of 5 than 1 or 2 results from gains in the entropy term (decrease to 4.64 from 5.54 or 6.57 kcal/mol in −TΔS) (Figure 3). These favorable significant changes in entropy are likely attributed to the replacement of ordered waters by the piperidine ring in the PDK2–5 structure (Figure 2b). Compared to 5, the presence of the asparagine moiety in 17 is apparently responsible to the large 3.4 kcal/mol gain in enthalpy change (ΔH) by the polar contacts in PDK2 (Figure 2c), despite the 2.7 kcal/mol loss in entropy (Figure 3).

protein.name: N-terminal His6-SUMO tagged recombinant human PDK2

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 50 mM MOPS, 50 mM KCl, 1 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM β-mercaptoethanol
